items.title: IonQ to Acquire Zero Trust Firm Elisity for Up to $1.3 Billion
items.summary: IonQ to acquire Elisity for up to $1.3 billion in an all‑stock deal. The acquisition adds Elisity’s least‑privilege access technology to IonQ’s security portfolio.

items.title: Inside AvisLoader: A Windows Malware Loader Built to Resist Disruption
items.summary: AvisLoader is a Windows malware loader that uses encrypted peer‑to‑peer communications to resist disruption. It employs ClickFix delivery, shortcut‑based persistence, and remote command execution.

items.title: Retail giant Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack
items.summary: Ahold Delhaize took some systems offline after a cybersecurity incident that impacted its network. The retailer is one of the world’s largest food chains.

items.title: Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex datacenters knock cloud and payments offline
items.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes hit Yandex data centers, knocking cloud and payment services offline and causing significant disruption to Russian digital services.

items.title: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
items.summary: The Bricksforge WordPress plugin vulnerability CVE‑2026‑85097 has been exploited in the wild, allowing attackers to take control of affected WordPress sites.

items.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
items.summary: GitLab warned users to patch a maximum‑severity code‑execution vulnerability in its CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on affected instances.

items.title: Passing the Baton: Dark Reading Names New Editor-in-Chief
items.summary: Dark Reading announced Fahmida Y Rashid as its new editor‑in‑chief, continuing the publication’s editorial direction.

items.title: Ukraine strikes third Yandex data center, disrupting digital services across Russia
items.summary: A third Yandex data center was struck by Ukrainian drones, shutting down and further disrupting cloud, payments, and delivery services across Russia.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Canonical Websites Disrupted in Second DDoS Attack This Year
items.summary: Canonical’s main Ubuntu and developer websites were disrupted by a second DDoS attack this year, affecting the Ubuntu blog and other official pages.

items.title: Microsoft: Windows 11 23H2 reaches end of support in 30 days
items.summary: Microsoft announced that Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise, Education, and IoT Enterprise editions will reach end of support in 30 days, ending security updates.

items.title: Major French Supermarket Chains Hit by Cyber-Attack, Food Stock Impacted
items.summary:
French supermarket chain Cooperative U confirmed a cyber-attack disrupted food inventory in multiple stores starting October 11.
The incident affected several outlets across the country.

items.title: Bring Your Own Agent: Your Employees' Assistants Are Already Logged In
items.summary:
Companies deploying personal AI assistants face security and privacy issues.
Amazon blocked Meta's Muse for not identifying as a bot, while Instinct raised privacy concerns.

items.title: Mastermind of 15,000-Mule Cybercrime Laundering Network Pleads Guilty in US
items.summary:
Oleg Korniev, leader of the YMCO money-laundering network, pleaded guilty in a U.S. court.
The network moved hacker funds abroad using 15,000 money mules.

items.title: Ledger Finds Unauthorized Hardware Implant in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallet Amid Fund Theft Reports
items.summary:
Ledger paused sales of CryptoBilis-distributed wallets after discovering unauthorized hardware implants.
The incident is linked to stolen funds totaling more than $86 million.

items.title: iRhythm Data Breach Impacts at Least 360,000 People
items.summary:
Hackers accessed personal data of at least 360,000 iRhythm patients.
The breach exposed names, addresses, emails, dates of birth, and phone numbers.

items.title: Microsoft’s new model helps AI agents judge their next move
items.summary:
Microsoft released a decision-scoring model that assigns calibrated probabilities to options.
The model supports routing, classification, and workflow control in secure applications.

items.title: Low-cost Android phones are arriving with malware that owners can’t uninstall
items.summary:
Bitdefender identified malware pre-installed on budget Android phones from various brands.
The malware ships in firmware before first use, making it hard to remove.

items.title: Critical SonicWall SMA 1000 Flaw Targeted in 135 Exploitation Attempts After Patch
items.summary:
Threat actors exploited a CVE-2026-102255 SSRF flaw in SonicWall SMA 1000 devices within days of patch.
135 exploitation attempts were observed.

items.title: Ransomware Response Expert Arrested in ShinyHunters FBI Hack Probe
items.summary:
Edward Dubrovsky, a Canadian cybersecurity executive, was arrested in the U.S. during an FBI probe of the ShinyHunters ransomware hack.
He was visiting the country for a conference.

items.title: Imagine there's no Shiny Hunters – AI could make human hacking crews obsolete
items.summary:
A discussion on The Kettle highlights arrests and a second bug exploited by Mythos.
It suggests AI could replace human hacking teams.

items.title: Net Closes Around ShinyHunters with Another FBI Arrest
items.summary:
FBI arrests Canadian cybersecurity executive linked to ShinyHunters.
The arrest is part of an ongoing crackdown on the group.

items.title: Your AI agent is only as safe as the packages it downloads
items.summary:
NVIDIA launches an agent safety platform that enforces security at the package level.
The platform still requires operators to vet the packages that are allowed.

items.title: Hidden implant in Ledger hardware wallets linked to $93M theft
items.summary:
Ledger discovered a hidden implant in hardware wallets that caused a $93 million theft via the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis.
The company says the damage is limited to confirmed cases.

items.title: Months-Old Palo Alto VPN Vulnerability Remains a Target for Ransomware Groups
items.summary:
Ransomware groups Qilin and Settra continue to exploit a Palo Alto VPN vulnerability patched in May.
The vulnerability remains a target for attackers.

items.title: Attackers Exploit CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
items.summary:
CVE-2026-85097 in the Bricksforge WordPress plugin is a CVSS 10.0 flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers upload and run arbitrary PHP code.
Active exploitation is reported.

items.title: Critical SonicWall Vulnerability Exploited Days After Disclosure
items.summary:
SonicWall devices are affected by CVE-2026-102255, a pre-authenticated SSRF flaw.
Attackers exploited the vulnerability within days of its disclosure.

items.title: Karaoke Giant Reveals Data Breach Impacting Eight Million
items.summary:
Daiichi Kosho disclosed a supply chain breach that exposed personal data of more than eight million karaoke customers.
The breach involved the company's data handling processes.

items.title: Let’s Encrypt Cuts Default Certificate Validity to 64 Days Ahead of 45-Day Switch
items.summary:
Let’s Encrypt will issue new certificates with a default validity of 64 days starting February 2027.
This precedes the planned switch to 45-day certificates.

items.title: Windows PCs missing key updates could lose security fixes in 2027
items.summary:
Microsoft warns that PCs lacking updated certificates will lose access to Windows Update after May 17 and June 19, 2027.
This could prevent delivery of security patches.

items.title: CyberXero Uses Claude Code in Campaign That Stole Over 628,000 Ukrainian Records
items.summary:
CyberXero used Anthropic's Claude Code to orchestrate AI-driven attacks on WordPress, e-commerce, and Ukrainian critical infrastructure.
The campaign stole more than 628,000 records.

items.title: Let’s Encrypt TLS certificate lifetimes to drop from 90 to 64 days starting February 2027
items.summary: Let’s Encrypt will reduce default TLS certificate validity from 90 to 64 days effective February 10, 2027. Existing 45‑ or 6‑day options remain unchanged. The final 90‑day certificate will expire May 11, 2027.

items.title: Geopolitics and the cyber resilience gap belong in your threat model
items.summary: World Economic Forum expert Akshay Joshi notes that AI, geopolitics, and industrialized fraud are reshaping cyber risk. CEOs now rank cyber‑enabled fraud above ransomware. The resilience gap between threat and defense is widening.

items.title: Strands Box: Open-source sandbox for AI agents
items.summary: AWS released Strands Box, an open‑source sandbox for AI agents that combines OS isolation with rule‑based action gating. It is currently in developer preview for Apple Silicon Macs; Linux support is planned. The tool addresses uncontrolled agent actions.

items.title: AI vulnerability patching has a grading problem
items.summary: Northwestern researchers tested AI coding agents on 112 real security bugs. With Claude Opus 4.7, one‑third of patches that fixed crashes failed maintainer tests. The study highlights reliability issues in AI‑generated vulnerability fixes.

items.title: What makes some open source updates so difficult?
items.summary: Google’s study shows maintaining internal copies of open source packages requires significant engineering effort. Most updates should take four hours or less, but many are more time‑consuming, indicating hidden costs of open source maintenance.

items.title: Nippon Columbia malware incident exposes 8.6 million karaoke fan records
items.summary: Malware infection at Nippon Columbia exposed over 8.7 million customer and employee records. Daiichi Kosho disclosed the incident and the scope of the data breach.

items.title: AI systems are fully capable of carrying out nightmare attacks against infrastructure and nobody's ready
items.summary: AI agents can manipulate robotic arms and falsify OT device operator screens. They can carry out infrastructure attacks. No organization is prepared for such capabilities.

items.title: Cyber exec arrested in case allegedly tied to ShinyHunters hackers
items.summary: Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky was arrested in Pennsylvania for alleged extortion tied to the FBI’s ShinyHunters crackdown.

items.title: ARTEX AI, Claude agents used in cyberattacks on South Korean banks
items.summary: A Chinese hacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite and Claude agents to launch cyberattacks on South Korean banks earlier this month.

items.title: Canadian cybersecurity executive arrested in federal extortion case
items.summary: A Canadian cybersecurity executive was arrested in a federal extortion case linked to the investigation of ShinyHunters’ attack on FBI IT systems.

items.title: Criminal IP Introduces AITEM as the Next Evolution of Attack Surface Management
items.summary: Criminal IP introduced AITEM, an AI‑powered attack surface management solution that connects exposure discovery with investigation, risk prioritization, and response.
